newsitem.title: USA: Rottlund Q1 backlog, orders lower.
newsitem.headline: Rottlund Q1 backlog, orders lower.

text.p: Rottlund Co Inc said Thursday backlog and new orders were lower at June 30, 1997, than a year earlier, citing tough comparisons in 1996.
Backlog at June 30, 1997 was 380 homes with a sales value of $57.4 million, 37 percent lower than the sales value of $90.8 million on a backlog of 638 homes at June 30, 1996.

New orders for 282 homes with a sales value of $39.2 million were received for the fiscal first quarter ended June 30, 1997, compared to 395 homes with a sales value of $59.6 million for the same period in 1996.

"The first quarter of fiscal 1998 was a difficult comparison for new orders versus record new orders from the previous year," said David Rotter, chief executive and president of Rottlund, citing fewer communities open for sales in our Minneapolis, Iowa and New Jersey markets.

"With the recent drop in interest rates, and the opening of fourteen additional communities in the next two quarters we expect new order comparisons to improve in the second half of the year," he added.
Rottlund on Thursday reported fiscal first quarter earnings of $0.08 a share versus $0.11. Rottlund designs, constructs and sells single-family homes, townhomes and villas.
